title: Elastic shadow headroom: predictive GPU memory budgeting for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal:
Implement a predictive GPU memory budgeting mechanism ("elastic shadow" headroom) that reliably balances utilization and OOM safety across three population sinks: model weights, KV cache, and transient activations produced by continuous batching. This ticket covers algorithm design, simulator validation, runtime allocator hooks, rollout plan, and dashboards/alerts.

Background:
- We see recurring transient OOMs when sustained KV growth aligns with large multi-tenant batch surges. Weights are mostly static per model. Activations vary with sequence length and batch shape from our continuous batching pipeline. Current static headroom rules are either wasteful (low load) or insufficient (bursts).

Proposed approach (Elastic Shadow Reservoir):
1) Forecast layer: short-horizon probabilistic forecasts for KV growth and batch-shape distribution. Inputs: EWMA of per-tenant prefix lengths, KV eviction/backpressure signals, recent batch-size histogram, queueing depth. Output: 1/10/60s quantile forecasts for KV bytes and activation peak.
2) Safety multiplier: map forecast quantiles to a safety margin via configurable policy (conservative, balanced, aggressive). Default = 97th percentile mapped to 1.15 multiplier.
3) Shadow reservoir: reserve a transient memory pool per-GPU and per-tenant that can be borrowed during bursts and reclaimed with graceful preemption (deferred preemption window = 100-300ms). The reservoir sits logically between weights (static) and activation/KV pools and is tracked in the allocator ledger.
4) Admission & preemption policy: continuous-batching admission consults the reservoir. When reservoir exhausted, admission either (a) delays batch partially (short defer), (b) routes to fallback model variant with lower activation footprint, or (c) triggers aggressive KV eviction policy. Defer + evict order decided by a cost function tuned per project.
5) Monitoring & safety nets: OOM detectors, soft-fails, and rollout guardrails. Built-in telemetry to measure reservoir utilization, reclaimed bytes/sec, preemption count, and tail-latency impact.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservatism vs utilization: higher safety multiplier reduces OOMs but increases cost. We will tune via simulated workloads and customers with bursty patterns.
- Complexity vs observability: adding a shadow pool increases runtime complexity; mitigated by detailed ledger metrics and a simulator.
- Preemption latency vs throughput: deferred preemption window reduces user impact but can allow transient overcommit; limits must be guarded by thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator shows >80% reduction in transient OOMs on representative burst traces with <5% median throughput regression and tail-latency increase <= 15% at P99 for normal traffic.
- Runtime integration passes end-to-end e2e tests and performance tests on staging fleet (no regressions in stable traffic).
- Dashboards with target metrics created and alerts for new failure modes (OOM rate, reservoir exhaustion rate, preemption events).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Design & simulator): finalize forecasting signals, safety mapping and cost function; deliver a deterministic simulator and run on three trace corpora. (owner: Jonas)
- M2 (Allocator hooks): add ledger accounting for shadow reservoir, provide APIs for borrow/reclaim, and wire preemption signal. (owner: Infra team)
- M3 (Admission policies): continuous-batching admission path consults reservoir; implement staged fallback (delay -> kv-evict -> route). (owner: Serving runtime)
- M4 (Telemetry & dashboards): expose metrics, create dashboard and alert runbook. (owner: Observability)
- M5 (Canary rollout): small fleet rollout, monitor, iterate, increase rollout % by health signals.

Risk & mitigation:
- Forecast drift: run conservative fallback and continuous model-retraining. Keep forecasts short-horizon.
- Ineffective eviction: add tenant-priority scoring and per-tenant soft limits.
- Reclaim thrash causing latency spikes: enforce min reclaim cadence and prioritize evicting cold KV segments.

Artifacts & references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Elastic+Shadow+Headroom+Design
- Initial simulator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7421
- Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rv-kv-memory/burst-sim

Notes from experiments so far:
- Early simulator runs on customer-trace A reduced OOMs by ~86% while lowering steady-state free memory by ~6 percentage points.
- Microbench on staging GPU nodes shows reservoir bookkeeping adds ~0.4% CPU overhead and 0.6% p99 extra latency in worst-case reclaim paths.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish simulator tuning & publish cross-team results (due 2025-11-08).
- Land allocator ledger PR and unit tests (target 2025-11-22).
- Prepare canary plan with rollback criteria and on-call contact (target 2025-11-29).
